title: connect() and write_transaction(): take the write lock up front
problem: Write the two building blocks every multi-process SQLite app needs: a connect() that waits for locks instead of failing at once and never opens hidden transactions, and a write_transaction() context manager that holds the write lock from its first line and always commits or rolls back.
requirements: connect(path, busy_timeout=5.0) returns a connection whose busy timeout is busy_timeout seconds
connect() opens no transactions implicitly (statements outside a transaction autocommit)
write_transaction(conn) starts a transaction that takes the write lock immediately, before any statement in the body
It commits when the body finishes and rolls back and re-raises when the body raises
The lock is released afterwards in both cases
contract: connect(path: str, busy_timeout: float = 5.0) -> sqlite3.Connection; write_transaction(conn) is a context manager
expectedBehavior: While `with write_transaction(a):` is open, another connection's BEGIN IMMEDIATE fails with 'database is locked', but its SELECTs still see the last committed data
edgeCases: The body raises: rollback, and the same exception propagates
The body writes nothing: the lock must still be held
busy_timeout given in seconds, reported by PRAGMA busy_timeout in milliseconds
hints: Conceptual: two sqlite3.connect() arguments do all of connect(). For write_transaction, remember from PY.M07 that code before `yield` is setup and code after it is cleanup; which kind of BEGIN takes the write lock at once?
Specific: connect needs timeout= and isolation_level=. In write_transaction, put the yield inside try/except so you can ROLLBACK and re-raise; COMMIT only when no exception happened.
Implementation: execute 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE', then try: yield conn / except BaseException: execute 'ROLLBACK'; raise. After the try block, execute 'COMMIT'.
evaluation: No hidden transaction state: conn.in_transaction is False after the block
